evidence: The agent confirmed config.rs reads LIVEKIT_API_KEY as required, so `claims.iss === "openconv"` hardcoded a deployment credential; ec7d20c routes `issuer: env.OPENCONV_LIVEKIT_ISSUER ?? "openconv"` through readHappyEnvironment instead of handing the script the key, which keeps the script credential-free as it is meant to be. The law token is a weak fit: neither the reviewer's shape nor the fix introduced a branch, so dataflow-vs-control-flow was not what was at stake.
guidance_note: When an acceptance script asserts on a value that the server reads from deployment config, take the expected value through the script's environment boundary from the start rather than baking in the currently observed value.

evidence: `const minted = await res.json()` threw before the check that reports status and body; the agent replaced the reviewer's status-gated parse with `mintOrNothing(body)`, correctly noting that a wrong host answers 200/405 HTML, so status is not the discriminator, and verified it with a wrong-host run that exits 1 without a stack trace.
guidance_note: When a script reads a live HTTP response, read it as text and parse it into the expected shape or null before any check, following the existing `mintConversation` pattern in web/conversation.js.

evidence: The inline `caller.roster().some((name) => name.startsWith("agent_"))` duplicated `isAgent` from web/conversation.js, which `caller.agentPresent()` already wraps; ec7d20c switches to `caller.agentPresent()`.
guidance_note: Before writing a predicate in a new client script, search the shared library it imports for an existing method that answers the same question.

evidence: The new script's own comment called `AUDIBLE_MS = 200` 'the same bar live-call-acceptance sets', which is a second copy; ec7d20c exports it from caller.mjs and both scripts import it. The agent correctly corrected the side claim: the existing `AUDIBLE = 1000` is an amplitude threshold, not this duration.
guidance_note: When a PR exists to extract one shared constant (the word list) from a sibling script, sweep the new script for every other value whose comment says it matches the sibling, and extract those in the same commit.

evidence: A bare `JSON.parse(readFileSync(keyPath))` failure does not name keyPath, while the next line's error does; ec7d20c wraps it to throw `${keyPath} is not JSON` with `cause`.
guidance_note: At a boundary parser, give every failure arm the same context, here the file path, as the arm right beside it.

evidence: The agent's node demo shows `Buffer.from(s, "base64")` decodes the URL-safe `-`/`_` alphabet identically on Node, so the S4 corrupted-bytes claim is wrong (the quoted warning concerns the browser's `atob`). Naming the encoding `base64url` to match webhook-delivery-acceptance.mjs is still correct, and the agent made that change while recording the correction.
guidance_note: When decoding a JWT segment, copy the encoding the sibling scripts already use (`base64url`) rather than relying on the decoder being lenient.

evidence: This duplicates F2 (unconditional `res.json()`); the same `mintOrNothing` fix in ec7d20c covers it, and it reports a non-JSON body rather than gating on `res.ok` as suggested.
guidance_note: When a script reads a live HTTP response, read it as text and parse it into the expected shape or null before any check.

evidence: This duplicates F3 (the inline `startsWith("agent_")`); ec7d20c's switch to `caller.agentPresent()` resolves both.
guidance_note: Before writing a predicate in a new client script, search the shared library it imports for an existing method that answers the same question.

evidence: The README listed minting among the things all three scripts share through caller.mjs, but the happy script mints with its own fetch and joins via `Caller.at()`; ec7d20c removes minting from the list and names the deliberate exception.
guidance_note: When a new script joins a README sentence that says 'all N scripts share X, Y, Z', check each listed item against the new script before raising the count.

evidence: The stop tested only `minted.allowed` while the check also required status 200, and neither required `conversationToken`, which `.split(".")` dereferenced next. ec7d20c folds all of these into one `usable` value read by both the check and the stop. That was the right choice, but its token condition (`typeof === "string"`) was too weak, which F12 then caught.
guidance_note: When a guard protects a dereference, make the guard establish exactly what the downstream code consumes (here, decoded claims) rather than a type test on the container.

evidence: live-call-acceptance records `caller.heard.error === null` to tell a crashed reader from silence, and the new script measured the same frames without it; ec7d20c adds the check, and the agent reports '696 frames read' on a run.
guidance_note: When writing a new script modeled on a sibling, diff the sibling's list of checks against the new one and justify every check left out.

evidence: ec7d20c's `usable` admits any string via `typeof minted?.conversationToken === "string"`, so `""` passes and `"".split(".")[1]` hands undefined to `Buffer.from`, the same crash F10's fix was meant to remove; the agent admits the earlier fix 'left one behind at this layer'. In 4c1c54d the agent parsed claims with `claimsOf` at the boundary instead of adding the suggested length-3 shape test, and verified it against eight malformed shapes.
guidance_note: When F10's guard was rewritten, it should have parsed the token into claims at the boundary; a type check on a value that is then split and decoded leaves the decode's own failure modes unguarded.

narrative: The round-0 review raised 11 findings on a new happy-server acceptance script. Two pairs were duplicates (F2/F7, F3/F8), and nearly all pointed at real gaps where the new script diverged from patterns its siblings and caller.mjs already set. The agent fixed everything in one commit, improved on several suggestions (mintOrNothing instead of status gating; issuer via env without taking the credential), and correctly downgraded the base64 S4 to a consistency fix with a Node demo. Its unified `usable` guard checked only that the token was a string, so round 1 found the empty-token crash (F12). The parse-at-boundary fix in 4c1c54d closed that, and round 2 approved.
guidance_observations: Most round-0 findings came from writing a sibling script without diffing it against live-call-acceptance and caller.mjs; a pre-PR pass comparing checks, constants, and predicates against the sibling would have removed about half the round.
The F12 round came from fixing F10 with a weaker guard than the downstream decode needed; parsing the claims in the first fix, as the agent eventually did, would have saved a review round.
Collapsing duplicate threads onto one fix and saying so on each thread kept the duplicate findings cheap.
